method.top10: Top 10 (new today first): the covered news stories (kind news) with a post in the 24 hours ending at the window end (pulse.py NOW, printed in BRT, UTC-3). First the stories first seen in that window (first seen = the earliest post in our sample), by heat; then the rest by heat, up to 10 in all. Ties break by the newest post (later first), then by stable id (ascending). Each row reads "new today" or "first seen <date>" (BRT date); every other story of the day keeps the same evidence record
method.records: evidence record (one per story; state proposed: the pipeline proposes no verdict and writes no label word, the owner confirms by PR): the stable story id, the computed fields it was built from (voices, posts per network, newsletters carrying it, official post, HN points, heat, complaint share, key words, topics), the status of each source, the method version and the config hash (first 16 hex of sha256 over the version, the method text and the sha256 of topics_lexicon.json, newsletters.json, official_feeds.json, indicators.json and hub_orgs.json). A network is fetched when one of its adapters read ok, partial when one read partial, else not fetched. A count reads "not fetched", never 0 or false, when no post of it was seen and its source was not fully fetched; official reads true when a lab or vendor feed posted the story and false only when the official feeds were fully fetched. Substance is the story's own links (its refs: GitHub repositories and arXiv papers its shown posts link to), its official post and its Hub check (method.hub); tracker samples of its topics read "related in topic" and never count as substance
method.gauges: gauges (at most four; each reads "preview, not yet reproducible" until 14 ledger days, a green recompute verifier and the owner's confirm; no trend line or arrow before 14 ledger days; no combined score). "Releases / research output by area" = papers published and repos created on the 7 UTC dates ending with the window end's, per tracker area, among the papers and repos in data.json (output volume, not capability); null when the tracker was not read in this run or its data is older than the window. "Hype vs substance" = for each Top 10 story its spread (voices, posts per network, newsletters, HN points) beside its substance (official post, own repo and paper links, models on the Hub under a listed organisation), components only, no ratio; null with no Top 10 story. "Daily movers" = the five topics whose rising ratio (conversation posts in the last day / daily average over 7 days; it needs 4+ conversation posts in 7 days and 2+ in the last day) is highest above 1 (up) and the five lowest below 1 (down), with all-network posts in 1 and 7 days for context; null when no topic has a reading or no conversation network was fetched. Below its floor a gauge is null with the reason; no value carries over from an earlier run. Coverage is the status of the sources a gauge reads. Risk (a dated, sourced event log, no dial) and Jobs read "no qualified source" until a qualified source exists; Jobs reads it for any change in jobs attributed to AI and carries context, not a forecast: the BLS series of indicators.json (latest month of each, preliminary flagged, and the same month a year earlier, as BLS publishes them) and, for the newest two Hacker News "Who is hiring?" threads, the top-level posts and those whose text names one of the AI terms of indicators.json. "Page views on Wikipedia (AI articles)" = user views (agent user, all access) of the fixed articles of indicators.json per project, summed over the 7 days ending with the newest day in the response and over the 7 days before them, both shown, no ratio; null for a project unless every listed article returned all 14 days. Page views are attention to an article, not awareness. Each source is read once per live run under one time budget; a source that failed reads null with its reason, never 0
method.hub: Hub check: a story with a release name (its label) is searched once on the Hugging Face Hub (models, the 100 most downloaded in 30 days whose id matches the name; a single word with no number is not searched); a model counts when its organisation is listed in hub_orgs.json (labs and vendors, never a person; admitted by the agent on 2026-10-18 under the owner's delegation, not yet reviewed by the owner, who vetoes by pull request) and its name carries the release name's words and numbers in order, a version exactly (Qwen 3 is not Qwen3.8). The record carries the count among those 100 and the five most downloaded matches (id, created, downloads in the last 30 days, likes); "no release name" when the story has none, "not fetched" when the search did not run or failed; 0 models is a reading of the listed organisations only, not a verdict that a model is closed, and a name that is not a model reads 0 too
